Read a tag specification sheet

Source: R/read_animals.R
read_tag_specs.Rd

Reads the tag specification sheet a manufacturer supplies with its tags into one row per transmitter: model, serial, life, the programmed delays, the power step, and for sensor transmitters the sensor type, unit, slope and intercept. The InnovaSea sheet ("Tag Summary", header row found by its names) is mapped, and so is a CSV with the same columns under shorter names, as labs often keep them: transmitter, tag_serial_number, tag_type, tag_life, min_delay_sec, max_delay_sec, sensor_type, units, slope and intercept.

Usage

read_tag_specs(file, col_map = NULL)

Arguments

file

Path to an InnovaSea tag specification sheet (.xls or .xlsx) or a CSV with its columns, or several such paths: each is read and the rows are bound, the first row of a transmitter kept.

col_map

Optional column map. A data frame, or the path to a CSV file, laid out as column_map() describes, replaces the packaged map. Pairs written as c(target = "source") are merged into the format's map: each replaces the rows of its target, and the other targets are read as the format reads them. A pair whose column is not in the file stops; column_map() gives the order in which a pair names the columns the format joins, as GLATOS joins two for transmitter.

Value

A data frame, one row per transmitter, with transmitter, tag_serial, tag_model, tag_life_days, min_delay, max_delay, power_level where the sheet gives it (the InnovaSea sheet does, the shorter CSV does not), sensor_type, sensor_unit, sensor_slope, sensor_intercept and sensor_type_raw, the sheet's own text of the sensor type. A tag programmed with several steps adds the step_

columns. With several files, the attribute source is a list of one record per file, and the column source_file names the file of each row.

Details

A file with no column for a tag's serial, model, life, delays or sensor calibration, such as a detection export or a deployment sheet, stops with an error that lists its columns, or the 5 nearest when it has 20 or more. For a workbook, these are the columns of its widest sheet. A Fathom VDAT CSV, which names its columns in a RECORD TYPE row and rows ending _DESC, gets an error that names it. The error says to read its detections, if it holds any, with read_detections(format = "vdat"), and its status records with read_receiver_logs(). A text file with no header row gets an error that says so.

The delays are those of the first step of the tag's programme. A tag programmed with several steps changes its delays over its life; the sheet's later steps are kept in the columns that start step_.

Sensor types written as one letter are read as "A" acceleration, "T" temperature, and "P" or "D" depth; words such as "pressure" or "predation (digestion)" are read as "depth" or "predation". The sheet's own text is kept in sensor_type_raw, and the attribute source counts the rows whose type read_tag_specs() could not class (sensor_type_unclassed, not counting "none"). Units are written as the contract spells them: "m", "C" and "m/s2".

See also

calibrate_sensors(), which takes the result as specs.

Examples

csv_file <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_tag_specs.csv", package = "detqc")
specs <- read_tag_specs(csv_file)
specs[, c("transmitter", "sensor_type", "sensor_unit", "sensor_slope")]
#>      transmitter sensor_type sensor_unit sensor_slope
#> 1 A69-1601-61001        <NA>        <NA>           NA
#> 2 A69-9002-61002       depth           m       0.1504
#> 3 A69-9002-61003       depth           m       0.1504
#> 4 A69-1601-61004        <NA>        <NA>           NA
